brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: 4 bases (piece:0,0,0, 1,0,0, 0,1,0 full; 0,-1,0 half-n) on one level, 8 parts in total. jointBolt:0#0,0#0 and #5 cleared the LOOSE_BODY warning. 15 open faces are left uncapped (info only).
drawer:0#0,-1#cut sits on the south cut face of half base piece:0,-1,0;half-n. It was placed from the only drawer offer, and the mesh check is clear.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet, holding a small platform
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 is a mount spike at the junction of the three full bases and carries platform-sm. A solid spike was refused for a platform (TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED), so I swapped it for the mount type.

finish.summary: Small single-level unit: three full bases in a triangle (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) with a half-north base at (0,-1) holding a drawer on its cut face. A mount spike stands where the three full bases meet and carries a small platform. Two joint bolts lock the bases. check_build found no rule errors and the mesh check is clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
